title: Projective geometric quotients of closed stable loci for PGL
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field], $r\geq1$ and $G=\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}$, the group scheme of invertible $r$ by $r$ matrices modulo scalars. Let $Z$ be a projective finite-type $k$-scheme [def-kun-projective, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with a $G$-action and an ample $G$-linearized invertible module $A$ [def-sc-invertible-module]; a linearization is an action on the line lifting the action on $Z$ and linear on fibres, and ample means that some positive tensor power gives a closed embedding into a finite-dimensional projective space. Write $Z^{ss}$ for the geometric points where some positive-degree $G$-invariant section of a power of $A$ is nonzero, and $Z^s$ for those semistable points having orbit closed in $Z^{ss}$ and stabilizer of dimension zero. Suppose $J\hookrightarrow Z^{ss}$ is a $G$-invariant closed subscheme contained in $Z^s$. Then there is a projective finite-type $k$-scheme $Q$ and a $G$-invariant surjection $q:J\to Q$ which is universal for $G$-invariant maps to algebraic spaces, and whose fibres on algebraically closed points are precisely the $G$-orbits. More precisely, for every algebraic space $B$ over $k$, composition with $q$ gives a bijection between maps $Q\to B$ and $G$-invariant maps $J\to B$, and for every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$ it gives $J(\Omega)/G(\Omega)\simeq Q(\Omega)$. If $\overline J$ is the scheme-theoretic closure of $J$ in $Z$, then $Q$ can be constructed as $\operatorname{Proj}(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}H^0(\overline J,A^{\otimes n}|_{\overline J})^G)$. The section-ring multiplication is [def-sc-invertible-section-ring] and $\operatorname{Proj}$ is [def-pc-proj]. This invariant graded algebra is finitely generated, and a sufficiently divisible Veronese subalgebra gives projectivity in the finite-projective-space convention. Algebraic spaces have the meaning in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. No linear reductivity or characteristic-zero hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Projective GIT quotient theorem, Chapter 1 Theorem 1.10, with reductivity in arbitrary characteristic (Haboush) and algebraic-space categorical universality of geometric quotients. Local book WANTED. Agent formulation of the closed stable-locus consequence; Morrison arXiv:0810.2340 Section 3.3 after Corollary 11 and Section 3.4 pp.17--18 describe this application, but do not prove this general algebraic-space quotient theorem.

proof.text: Form the scheme-theoretic image, with its open immersion from J. Noetherianity gives quasi-compactness. Apply the invariant-image restriction and its semistability comparison.

The image inclusion pulls back the ambient semistable open into the range of J by the closed-range image lemma. Lift geometric points through the open immersion J→X. Cancellation of the closed immersion transfers stable orbits and stabilizers to X.

Apply invariant section finiteness to X. Convert finite algebra generators to the ambient-subring definition IsFinitelyGenerated. Interpret the additive grading as k-submodules; compare the two Proj schemes by identity graded homomorphisms. The finite-graded-Proj theorem gives the Veronese, finite-type, quasi-compactness and projective embedding clauses.

Apply affine quotient gluing to the semistable open J of X. Transfer invariance, algebraic-space universality and geometric orbit equivalence back to the ambient action using restriction compatibility and cancellation of the closed immersion.

proof_origin.place: T6 implementation of the image, finite graded Proj, and affine-chart quotient assembly of GIT Chapter 1 Theorem 1.10. New supporting statements retain the original source route.

Steps: 1 restricts the action to the closure via the cited flat-density lemma (J→X is qcqs and dense; G×X→X is flat). 2-3 show X^ss = X∩Z^ss = J by graded power lifting on Sym(T_an)→Sym(S_an) and the equivariant multiplication to T, with no exactness of invariants assumed. 4 gives finitely generated R=S^G with finite-dimensional R_0, so Proj R is projective. 5 takes the X_s charts. 6 proves R_(s) ≅ S_(s)^G with zero divisors allowed (the defect is killed by s^m). 7 checks the affine-node hypotheses on J_s (orbits closed in the invariant open, stabilizers unchanged). 8 glues via t^d/s^e. 9 gives universality through the Zariski-sheaf property of algebraic spaces. 10 gives the orbit bijection. New nodes are true: PGL reductivity, finite generation and graded power lifting; affine closed-orbit finite-stabilizer quotient, categorical for all algebraic spaces through finite inertia and Keel–Mori; section-algebra package (0B5T(1),(3),(4), 0EKE, qcqs fraction iso); Veronese projectivity of a finitely generated graded algebra with finite-dimensional R_0 (Proj R^(d) = Proj k[R_d] in P^N_k). Edge cases checked: empty, r=1, R_+=0, nonreduced, char p. Not a restatement split. Advisory: when the section-algebra node is split, cite lem-sc-section-ring-localization-bijective. Tool use: lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback (sec-nagata) for step 1.
